title: MWCC codegen facts explain a difference; they never justify a fakematch
summary: These GC/1.2.5 facts, and the rayanht/mwcc compiler sources (`real_code_evidence compiler --query <term>`), explain a codegen difference so you can find what the original source wrote; an explanation is never permission for a fakematch, and codegen facts from TP, TWW, MKDD or AC do not transfer (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md).

Colouring order: vregs are numbered arguments in parameter order, named locals in reverse order of declaration, then compiler @NNN objects; nodes with degree below 29 are pushed in ascending number and coloured in reverse, each taking a free volatile or already used callee-saved register before a new one from r31 down. So the first-declared local holds the highest callee-saved register, every compiler object outranks every named local, and inside an inline expansion the order flips.

Degree limit: `this` in r31 instead of r28 with every instruction matching means `this` (12 physical neighbours plus every live vreg) reached degree 29 at 17 vregs and was coloured first; one vreg more or less in the original moves it.

A coalesced node (a value that goes straight into an argument register) is never pushed and adds one to every neighbour's degree; a variable that gets a new value starts a new web, numbered as a high compiler object.
IRO_CommonSubs creates a CSE value at the second occurrence of its expression, so a value read at the top and again in the last statement is numbered low and coloured last.

An inline binds each argument it cannot repeat safely (a call, a forced load) and the bindings run last parameter first, so a ROM that evaluates two complex arguments in source order had them the other way round in the parameter list.

Inline passes: pass 0 expands the calls the source writes with no size limit; pass 1 (calls a pass-0 expansion uncovered) takes callees of at most 10 statements, pass 2 at most 7, pass 3 at most 3, and there is no pass 4; a call in the argument of an expanded call is one pass deeper. A `bl` to a trivial inline right after the same inline was expanded, with a weak copy in the TU, means the original had one more inline level above that call.
qa_enforcement: review; worker guidance with no lint
do: Name the compiler mechanism and the source evidence for the real fix in the attempt summary.
do_not: Submit a declaration reorder, reused variable or extra local whose only support is a register change (sms-no-steering).
provenance: Added 2026-10-17 from doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md and AGENTS.md (objectives/worker-compiler-loop plan section 3.4.4). Facts are restated as diagnosis; upstream tactics the SMS policy bans (volatile frame probes, TODO or fabricated markers, temporary pragmas, wrappers and marker calls, frame levers) are not carried.

title: Reference: upstream MWCC codegen and evidence facts (not injected)
summary: SMS builds with MWCC GC/1.2.5 (GC/1.2.5n for a few SDK units), and every sms_compiler fact was measured on SMS with it. Codegen facts from TP, TWW, MKDD or AC never transfer, because each uses another MWCC version: take only source-level facts from them (names, field order, control flow, whether a function or an assert existed). (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#mwcc-matching-tips-for-agents; AGENTS.md#other-games)

Read the compiler instead of guessing spellings: rayanht/mwcc is a 100% matching decompilation of mwcceppc.exe that covers GC/1.2.5, usually at ../mwcc next to the checkout. Search it with `real_code_evidence compiler --query <term> [--path Coloring.c|src/backend]`: src/frontend (CInline.c, CExpr.c, CMangler.c) for inlining and mangling, src/optimizer/Iro*.c for CSE and propagation, src/backend (Coloring.c, InterferenceGraph.c, StackFrameEABI.c, Peephole.c) for registers, frame slots and peephole. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#read-the-compiler-instead-of-guessing-the-mwcc-decompilation; docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#use-the-compiler-sources-and-the-mwcc-debugger)

A compiler explanation tells you what the original source must have contained; it is never permission for a fakematch, and every sms_baseline and sms_fidelity rule still applies. Confirm each conclusion with a real SMS build. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#read-the-compiler-instead-of-guessing-the-mwcc-decompilation)

Work on differences in this order: control flow and call order, then the order of loads and stores, then instruction selection, then registers, then the frame. Registers and the frame often follow once the first three are right, and the unnamed @NNN objects of a correct inline change register colouring, so a register difference says little until the inline depth is right. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#priority-order, #what-not-to-focus-on-first)

Upstream lets humans keep marked scaffolding; the SMS harness is stricter and never submits TODO or fabricated markers, temporary pragmas, wrappers, marker calls or volatile frame probes (sms-no-agent-comments, sms-fabricated-marker, sms-no-steering, sms-temporary-tactics). (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#mindset, #matching-workflow-for-agents)

A body in a .cpp is inlinable only with at most 15 statements and 1024 bytes of locals (CInline_IsSmallFunction); the verdict belongs to the callee, so a difference between two sites of one callee never comes from its body. Count: an initialized declaration 1, `if (c) x;` 2, a release-stripped JUT_ASSERT 1, while or for 4, return (also the implicit one) 1, a bare declaration 0. A body inside the class body has no gate; a class-template member defined outside the class is never inlined. If the ROM inlines what our build calls, the original body had 15 statements or fewer, often because a block was a call to a helper the map names. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#is-the-callee-inlinable-at-all, #an-in-class-body-has-no-gate)

Inline passes: pass 0 expands the calls the source writes with no size limit, pass 1 (calls that a pass-0 expansion uncovered) takes callees of at most 10 statements, pass 2 at most 7, pass 3 at most 3, and there is no pass 4; a call in the argument of an expanded call is one pass deeper. A `bl` to a trivial inline a few instructions after the same inline was expanded, with a weak copy in the TU, means the original had one more inline level above that call. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#the-inline-pass-ladder)

A pass-0 call stays a `bl` only in a conditional part (right operand of &&, || or comma, an arm of ?:) when the callee has control flow, as the full expression of return, if or switch when the callee returns early, when it came from a deeper pass over budget, or as a virtual call; argument shape, `Class::f` against `this->f` and body position never change the verdict. A zero-argument call of a constructor with default arguments goes through a synthesized wrapper and costs one pass. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#why-a-pass-0-call-can-stay-a-bl, #a-zero-argument-call-of-a-constructor-with-default-arguments-costs-one-pass)

Where MWCC did not inline, it emitted a weak or local copy that mario.MAP lists: that copy is the original body, and its shape is evidence (two blr and no join is an `if` with an early return; a ternary never gives that). A pointer that m2c reloads from the same lookup before each operation marks an inlined wrapper (DSPInterface::setPauseFlag(ch, 1) for getDSPHandle(ch)->setPauseFlag(1)); find the wrapper in the map or a header. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#look-at-the-out-of-line-copies-before-you-change-an-inline, #a-getter-that-repeats-before-every-operation-is-a-wrapper-inline)

MWCC never moves loads, stores and calls relative to each other and never removes a write: each ROM store is a source store, in that order. A call, or a store through a pointer, drops cached loads, so where the ROM loads a value again shows where the original had a call or an indirect store between the two reads. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#mwcc-does-not-reorder, #mwcc-removes-redundant-reads-never-writes)

Member-load CSE follows the spelling, not the address: a read inside an inlined accessor is bound to that call's temp, so a second lwz of a member that could have stayed in a register points at an inline accessor at one of the two reads; a member at offset 0 is never a CSE candidate, `const` on an inline's pointer parameter stops the merge, and IRO_CommonSubs creates the shared value at the second occurrence of its expression, never the first. Such an accessor stays a hypothesis until sms-accessor-evidence holds. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#where-member-load-cse-happens, #an-inline-accessor-breaks-member-cse, #const-on-an-inlines-pointer-parameter-stops-cse, #when-cse-temps-are-born)

MWCC numbers vregs: arguments in parameter order, then named locals in reverse order of declaration, then front-end @NNN objects (a later one gets a lower number), then back-end ones. simplifygraph pushes nodes whose degree is below 29 GPRs in ascending number, and colorgraph pops them, each taking the lowest free volatile register or an already used callee-saved one before a new callee-saved register counting down from r31. So the first-declared named local holds the highest callee-saved register, every unnamed compiler object outranks every named local, and r0 is never a load or store base. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#how-mwcc-colours-registers)

A rotated callee-saved block with every instruction matching says the original declared its locals in another sequence; inside an inline expansion it flips (the last-declared local of the inlined body holds the highest register), and bound arguments of an inline run last parameter first, so a ROM that evaluates two complex arguments in source order had them the other way round in the parameter list. This is a reading of the original that needs evidence, never an edit to submit on its own (sms-no-steering). (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#local-declaration-order-picks-the-callee-saved-registers, #inside-an-inline-expansion-the-order-flips, #bound-arguments-run-last-parameter-first)

`this` in r31 instead of r28 with every instruction matching is the degree limit: `this` is live for the whole function, so its degree is 12 plus the live vregs, and at 17 vregs it reaches 29, waits for a later sweep, is coloured first and gets r31. A coalesced node (a value that goes straight into an argument register) is never pushed and adds one to each neighbour's degree, and a variable that gets a new value starts a new web, numbered as a high temp. These count nodes in the original: look for the real construct that adds or removes one (a real global accessor, a proven helper, a variable the original reused). (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#the-degree-limit-this-in-r31-instead-of-r28, #coalesced-nodes-raise-every-neighbours-degree, #the-first-web-and-later-webs)

Frame facts are diagnostics only: SMS stops at the stack frame (sms-temporary-tactics), and a frame deficit is never evidence for a spelling. frame = round8(8 + round8(locals) + 4 x saved GPRs + 8 x saved FPRs); each inline expansion keeps a slot for an expression receiver, each expression argument, a non-void return and each named local of its body, even after the optimizer deletes every instruction that used it. A frame that is too small usually means more or deeper inline expansions in the original at the same instructions, rarely a missing local; one that is too big means fewer. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#frame-arithmetic, #what-reserves-a-slot; AGENTS.md#frame-deficits-are-not-evidence)

Most game units build with `-inline deferred`, so their functions are defined in reverse map order; the src/JSystem/JAudio units do not use it and follow the map forward, and there MWCC can inline a helper only into a function defined later, so only symbols below an UNUSED entry can be its callers. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#-inline-deferred-and-the-order-of-definitions; AGENTS.md#important-things-to-keep-in-mind)

Sections: an explicitly sized array of 8 bytes or less can go to .sdata, an unsized array always goes to .data, and const-ness moves a global between sections. An anonymous aggregate literal from a header inline compiled in the PCH lands in .data, the same literal in a .cpp in .rodata, so a .data constant where ours is .rodata means the original called the header inline. Original section size = linked size in the map + the UNUSED sizes in that section. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#sections)

A function-local static with a non-trivial initializer emits pos$NNN plus a 1-byte guard init$NNN, which is never a separate static bool; statics inside an inline are named <name>$localstatic<N>$<mangled function>, with the developer's own variable name. @unnamed@ marks an anonymous namespace (a local symbol without it is a plain static), and a qualified (func,local) map entry is a static function in a namespace or a template instance, never a class member. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#function-local-statics-initnnn-is-the-guard, #mangling)

Literals, labels, unnamed compiler objects and local classes share one @NNN counter, so the gap between two @NNN numbers counts what the source made between their first uses (an extra inline level 1 per site, `if (c)` 2, if/else 3, while 4, each extra && or || term 1, plain statements and literals 0). It narrows candidates for the same instructions, but several sources give the same count, so it never proves one alone. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#the-unique-id-counter)

Implicit class-template members are weak and land in every TU that sees the body; the `>>>` lines in mario.MAP's closure show which TUs emitted each weak symbol. A whole-function asm definition turns off both peephole passes for every later function in its TU (no record-form rlwinm. and no lbzu/stbu after it). (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#templates, #an-asm-function-turns-off-the-peephole; AGENTS.md#the-maps)

Evidence, strongest first: a name in mario.MAP (a function, a data symbol, or a class inside a mangled signature); a debug string in the binary (PARAM_INIT field names, an assert condition); a setter that stores the field; an allocation size (count * sizeof(T) names the array it fills); the parameter name of the function the value goes to; the size of an UNUSED map symbol. A guess that compiles to the right bytes is not evidence: many sources compile to the same bytes. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#what-counts-as-evidence)

A name in our own source is not evidence: a local, placeholder or field name that someone wrote earlier (often an agent in the same session) is a guess, so never read it back as proof. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#what-counts-as-evidence)

symbols.txt lists only what survived in the DOL: grep mario.MAP for the mangled name before calling a function inline, stripped or missing. The closure part of mario.MAP (before `.init section layout`) has a `>>>` line for each other TU that emitted the same weak symbol, so the closure, not the section layout, shows which TUs emitted an inline. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#the-maps)

marioL.MAP links about 287 functions that mario.MAP calls UNUSED, and the entries one level under a function in its closure tree are that function's call list; maps of other versions (orig/GMSP01/files/marioEU.MAP, orig/GMSJ01_01/files/mario.MAP) can name functions the JP map does not, usually the same source dead-stripped from the JP link. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#the-maps)

Other games give source-level facts only: names, field order, control flow, whether a function or an assert existed. Trace a borrowed name back to a shipped map or a string in that game's binary (a decomp's asm and symbols.txt are its own naming decisions, and Luigi's Mansion has no map); SMS's own map wins on names and on inline-or-not. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#other-games)

A high match percentage does not mean correct behaviour: objdiff ignores register names and scores a changed offset as a small difference, and real gameplay bugs hid in 97-99.8% functions (a field load at the wrong offset, a wrong mask bit or compare constant, the wrong vtable slot, callee or receiver, two values stored into each other's slots, a misplaced brace, `max` where the ROM has `min`). Check the data flow of every `~` line: which offset feeds which store, which register is the receiver, which arm writes the result. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#important-things-to-keep-in-mind)

Prove every hunk: revert each change on its own, rebuild, and keep only real fixes that move the object toward the target; follow the file's own idioms (a form that no already-matching function in the same file or directory writes is usually a fakematch); when two spellings both match, choose the one that invents nothing (a plain local beats a new helper, and a map-proven helper beats an unproven one). (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#matching-workflow-for-agents)

Frame deficits are never evidence: two f32 pads, two s32 pads, one f64, four u16s or two pointers give the same 100%, and an invented accessor almost always gives the missing slots too, so a frame match says nothing about what the original wrote. Remove every pad and probe before measuring anything else in a function: a pad sets the frame, so a correct candidate measures worse next to it. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#frame-deficits-are-not-evidence)

The accessor consistency test: an accessor with no map symbol is a hypothesis, so test it at every site in the game that touches that member and read the whole changes_all report. A real accessor holds everywhere and no function gets worse; if any function gets worse the hypothesis is refuted and you remove it; never keep it only at the sites where it helps (that is choosing by score); an accessor that changes nothing anywhere has no evidence either. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#the-accessor-consistency-test)

A helper the ROM proves (its out-of-line copy matches byte for byte, or the map names it) is used at every site whose code it explains, even where a match percentage drops. A class's own methods read its own fields raw, so never add a getter for a class's own field inside that class. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#the-accessor-consistency-test, #frame-deficits-are-not-evidence)

Upstream sweep verdicts: TFlagManager::getInstance(), SMSGetMarDirector(), TMarDirector::getConsole(), getGamePad(N) and J3DModelData::getVtxPosArray() are real; SMSGetMarioParticleManager(), SMSGetMap() and TParamVec::set are refuted (read gpMarioParticleManager and gpMap raw); TPlacement::getPosition() never closes a frame deficit, since thousands of matching functions read mPosition raw. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 docs/AGENT_MATCHING_TIPS.md#known-accessor-verdicts)

marioL.MAP links about 287 functions that mario.MAP calls UNUSED, and the entries one level under a function in its closure tree are its call list; it and the reference projects help recover an inlined body, but they do not replace the same-TU inline test above (the SMS maintainer rule is stricter than upstream's). (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#never-fabricate-an-unused-body, #decide-fast-whether-an-unused-body-is-recoverable)

An exact map size is a necessary check on a body that came from evidence, never a reason to believe a guessed body, so do not tune a guess to the size. Stronger is the weak helper cluster: MWCC emits the weak helpers a function first needs right after it, so the run of weak symbols after an UNUSED map entry fingerprints its body (a __dt__ means a by-value local of that type, __construct_new_array means new T[n], a run of one class's accessors means the body touched that class). Subtract the delete tail before sizing a destructor: an empty one is already about 0x70 bytes. (doldecomp/sms@4641b450 AGENTS.md#never-fabricate-an-unused-body)
